neighbours.label: a word for a bodily act or medical procedure on the body (sit, amputate, vomit), as against other verbs in the same sentences
fire: After the crash the surgeons had to amputate his left foot.
The old priest could no longer kneel and had to sit during the service.
The medicine made her vomit twice before breakfast.
Frostbite was so bad that two of his toes were amputated.
The doctor asked him to sit on the bench and breathe slowly.
Some children vomit on long bus journeys over the mountains.
His injured arm was amputated below the elbow in the field hospital.
Too weak to stand, the old man had to sit in a chair at the wedding.
quiet: After the crash the mechanics had to replace his left tyre.
The old priest could no longer read and had to listen during the service.
The medicine made her sleepy twice before breakfast.
Frostbite was so bad that the expedition was cancelled.
The doctor asked him to wait in the hall and read a magazine.
Some children sing songs on long bus journeys over the mountains.
His injured arm was bandaged below the elbow in the field hospital.
Too tired to dance, the old man had to watch the wedding from afar.
